In 1 minute

Engagement survey action plans

Paulo · Employee Engagement Specialist

A software company with 640 people and 71 managers requires an action plan within 30 days of the engagement survey.

When it runs
Release of results by team in the engagement tool, about 10 days after the semiannual survey closes; one plan per manager with a team of 8 or more respondents
What it delivers in production
Within 2 business days each manager gets a draft with up to 3 actions justified by their own team's numbers. The manager approves or swaps them, and the approved plan lives on the team's Notion page.
Who decides
Proposes the draft; the manager approves
Effort
Calibrate on 30 previous plans; two weeks
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output

# Post-survey action plan rules

Current cycle: 2026-H2. Results released on 2026-11-16.

## When a dimension triggers the rule
- Favorability below 65%, or a drop of 10 points or more (change_points equal to or less than -10).
- The 8 dimensions: Recognition, Priority clarity, Autonomy, Development, Well-being, Collaboration, Leadership, Compensation.

## How to choose the action
1. Order: triggered dimension with the lowest favorability first.
2. Possible action: prerequisite "none" or a ritual the team has in rituals_calendar.csv (same text, for example "biweekly retro").
3. Among the possible ones, the one with the highest avg_effect. If it goes over the total of 12 hours, the next one that fits.
4. At most 3 actions per team. A triggered dimension left over goes to "Next cycle".
5. Action not done in the previous plan: use another possible one of the same dimension. If there is no other, repeat it and mark REPEATED.
6. Prerequisite "compensation team decision": outside the manager's approval authority. It goes to "Not proposed, forwarded to the compensation team", never to the list.
7. Owner: the team's manager. Deadline: the library's. Usage history: teams_that_applied and avg_effect in points.

## Standard insufficient-sample message
"Insufficient sample: fewer than 8 respondents. The plan by dimension is not generated and the manager receives only the department average."

## Draft destination
- Normal: to the manager, AWAITING APPROVAL.
- Dimension below 40%: signal to the culture team for a conversation with the manager before sending.
- Drop of 20 points or more: the draft goes first to the culture team.

## Rules with no leeway
- A team with fewer than 8 respondents receives only the standard message: no percentage, no action and no alert to the culture team. E.g.: Support Tier 2, 6 respondents, even with Well-being at 30%.
- A drop counts even with favorability above 65%. E.g.: Cloud Infrastructure, Priority clarity 70% with -12.
- 12-hour cap: E.g.: Cloud Infrastructure adds 6h + 4h = 10h; the all-hands highlight (3h) would go over 12h, so the written feedback in the 1:1 (2h) goes in, total 12h.
- Prerequisite: E.g.: Payments Platform has no biweekly retro, so the priorities board does not work and the written summary after the all-hands goes in, which was not done in the previous cycle: REPEATED.
- No sentence compares one manager with another or qualifies the leadership. Only dimension and number.

## Excluded excerpt
Whatever a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## Single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and write the file to Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, draft, write). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A team with fewer than 8 respondents gets no plan and the manager sees only the department average, because with 5 responses favorability by dimension becomes individual opinion. Nothing is published without the manager's acceptance. An action on compensation, promotion or termination is routed to the responsible team, never proposed to the leader. The agent does not rank managers or attribute low results to leadership: it describes dimension and number.

Common mistakes

  • Proposing an action for every dimension below the company average; half the teams will always be below, and the manager gets 8 actions and does none.
  • Reading a 10-point drop in a team that replaced 4 people in the semester as worse engagement; the respondent base changed.
  • Accepting 'improve communication' as an action, with no owner, deadline and ritual where it happens.
  • Repeating the same action in the next cycle without checking whether the previous one was completed.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Managers with a plan logged within 30 daysfrom 46% to 85% or moreestimate based on the described routine
Culture team hours in results walkthrough meetingsfrom about 120 hours per cycle to 30 to 40 hoursestimate based on the described routine
Actions with updated status at 90 daysfrom 40% to 75% or moreestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Payments Platform team, manager Ana, 11 of 12 respondents, cycle 2026-H2.
Dimensions that triggered the rule: Recognition 48% favorable (company 71%), down 14 points; Clarity of priorities 55% (company 68%), stable.
Proposed actions, total effort 9h in the quarter:
1. Recognition | Spotlight round at the monthly all-hands with 1 team deliverable named by the manager | 3h | owner: Ana | deadline: 3 months | 6 teams applied it, favorability rose 9 points
2. Clarity of priorities | Board of the quarter's 3 priorities reviewed at the biweekly retro | 4h | owner: Ana | deadline: 6 weeks
3. Recognition | Written feedback in a 1:1 for each person by the end of the quarter | 2h | owner: Ana
Not proposed: compensation action, outside the manager's authority and routed to the compensation team.
Status: AWAITING APPROVAL from the manager in Slack. Previous plan: 2 of 3 actions completed.
